The meal that comes second in the day, after breakfast, is lunch.

In the text provided, the author’s motive is to explore themes of human connection and the natural cycle of life and decay through a botanical metaphor. This motive is structurally linked to the narrative arc where the protagonist’s emotional state (sadness and isolation) is mirrored by the physical state of the sunflower (wiltng). By aligning the protagonist’s internal struggle with the external decay of the plant, the author emphasizes the impact of neglect on both nature and personal relationships, thereby reinforcing the thematic structure of interconnectedness and consequence.
